classification.difficultyReason: Locate each zero of the absolute-value argument and sketch two upward branches with gradients -1 and 1; recognise that |3-x|=|x-3| when positioning the final vertex.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of the following.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex $(0,0)$ and branch gradients $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Upward V at the origin; ungridded axes and branch arrowheads.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex $(2,0)$, $y$-intercept $2$, and branch gradients $-1$ and $1$.
answer.worked:
$$y=\begin{cases}2-x,&x<2,\\x-2,&x\geq2.\end{cases}$$
The branches meet at $(2,0)$ and pass through $(0,2)$.

spec.description: Upward V with vertex at x=2 and y-intercept 2; no grid.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex $(-1,0)$, $y$-intercept $1$, and branch gradients $-1$ and $1$.
answer.worked:
$$y=\begin{cases}-x-1,&x<-1,\\x+1,&x\geq-1.\end{cases}$$
The branches meet at $(-1,0)$ and pass through $(0,1)$.

spec.description: Upward V with vertex x=-1 and y-intercept 1; no grid.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex $(3,0)$, $y$-intercept $3$, and branch gradients $-1$ and $1$.
answer.worked:
$$y=\begin{cases}3-x,&x\leq3,\\x-3,&x>3.\end{cases}$$
The branches meet at $(3,0)$ and pass through $(0,3)$.

spec.description: Upward V with vertex x=3 and y-intercept 3; no grid.
